_comment: Config sections only the HOST process may write, and what dropping them does.
Every config.save that arrives over the hub bus — a remote/web client, a plugin,
or an agent through the MCP facade — is by definition not from the host, so these
sections are stripped before the merge. `updates` earns its place: updates.channel
is concatenated into the electron-updater feed URL the desktop then downloads and
installs from, so one '../' in a channel relocates the updater to somebody else's
repo — persistent code execution laundered through the app's own update dialog.
Both bus entry points must agree: the Go brain (dropHostTrusted, the default under
DELEGATE_CATALOG_TO_BRAIN) and the desktop's own bus handler (hubCapabilities.ts).
The desktop's in-process Settings write does NOT go through either and is unaffected.
Drop is by top-level section: a whole section goes or stays, never a sub-key.

cases.name: a host-trusted section is dropped, the rest is kept
the traversal payload this exists to stop
a partial with nothing host-trusted passes through untouched
the whole section goes even when it carries innocuous keys too
a null-valued host-trusted section is still a write attempt
